main_topics.reason: The user opened with pain returning three months after surgery and came back to why it recurred so fast.
The opening question was whether another surgery is needed, and the user later asked when surgery would be considered.
Several turns covered alternatives to the pill, with the user asking specifically about the hormonal IUD and mood effects.
The user explained they stopped the pill because of low mood and no libido, which shaped the options discussed.
The user said they felt defeated and later said they felt less hopeless and valued being taken seriously.
The user engaged with the new idea that pain may not be all endometriosis, over a few turns.
The user had not taken in the surgery findings and welcomed the idea of requesting the note.
The user mentioned once that they were given no hormonal treatment and only told to come back if problems arose.

output.summary: A user whose endometriosis pain returned three months after laparoscopy asked whether they need more surgery. The bot explained recurrence, hormonal options such as the hormonal IUD given they did not tolerate the pill, when repeat surgery is considered, and possible pelvic floor involvement, then gave a three-step plan. The user said it was clear and that they felt less like it was 'surgery forever'.
